summary: Unexpected latency increase in EU interactive sessions after enabling region-affinity setting
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a sudden rise in interactive-chat p95 latency (~300–450ms delta) for users routed to eu-west and eu-central after they turned on the "region-affinity" preference for their account. Impact: Production users of MuseAI (dedicated tenant) observe degraded interactive responsiveness for chat features; request rate unchanged. Environment: prod - eu-west, dedicated pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Customer toggled 'region-affinity' in the Console for their tenant at 2026-03-08T14:12Z. 2) Observe interactive chat p95 on their service dashboard and external synthetic clients. 3) Toggle back to 'any-region' and re-measure. Observed behavior: With affinity enabled, p95 increased by ~320ms for eu-west requests and ~280ms for eu-central for ~45 minutes after the change. Toggling back to any-region returned p95 to baseline within 10 minutes. Logs & traces: Edge logs show intermittent additional NAT hops and occasional TLS handshake timeouts to backends in eu-west-2. Control-plane audit shows residency preference change propagated to two control-plane nodes at different times (2026-03-08T14:12Z and 2026-03-08T14:18Z). Customer timeline and screenshots attached to the ticket via email (not included in JSON).
comments: Support (Liam): Received initial report and collected synthetic trace links and timestamps from customer. Escalated to SRE and assigned to Priya.
SRE (Priya): Started by checking control-plane propagation logs and edge-proxy routing tables; noted discrepancy in stamp propagation to eu-west edge cluster A vs B.
Customer (Nina, MuseAI): Confirms toggling affinity off returns performance to normal; can reproduce with our synthetic clients in eu-west.
SRE (Priya): Requested tenant ID and sample request IDs; asked customer not to toggle setting until we capture traces. Customer provided tenant:muse-428 and sample request ids.
Support (Liam): Logged internal INT-4412 to investigate edge stamp propagation race-condition. Linked PR to infra change that rolled out two days prior.
SRE (Priya): Noted known infra rollback candidate: PR #3283 touched control-plane caching TTLs; correlates with the timeframe. Will run packet captures and a short canary traffic test in eu-west-2.
SRE (Priya): Found that some edge nodes attempted fallback to secondary egress (us-west) for a subset of sessions during propagation window, adding cross-region RTT. Collecting full pcap and spans.

Support (Liam): Informed customer of active investigation and recommended a temporary rollback to any-region if immediate mitigation needed. Customer requested we attempt to fix before forcing config change on their side.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Control-plane residency stamp update propagated non-atomically to edge clusters, causing mixed-ejection to secondary egress for sessions established during window.
Hypothesis 2: Edge proxy cache TTL reduced by infra change (PR #3283) resulting in stale residency states and more frequent TLS re-handshakes to fallbacks.

Finding: Correlated timestamps show control-plane wrote new residency stamp at 2026-03-08T14:12Z but global edge invalidation completed at 2026-03-08T14:17:45Z; during that 5m45s window, ~12% of requests were routed via a secondary egress in us-west, adding ~280–400ms RTT.
Trace excerpt: span IDs [span:0a3f, span:0a4b] show extra hop eu-west-edge -> nat-gw-us-west -> eu-west-backend; TLS handshake retries observed in 1.4% of affected requests.
Load/Capacity: Dedicated GPU pool healthy; no autoscale events or GPU contention observed during window.

Related change: PR https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3283 reduced control-plane cache flush parallelism, intended to reduce DB write pressure, but inadvertently increased propagation variance under low load.
SRE action: Collected packet captures and request-level traces; created filtered logs and uploaded to secure S3 for eng review (link provided to engineers only).
resolution_notes: Workaround: Temporarily switching the tenant to 'any-region' restored baseline latency within ~10 minutes and is a validated mitigation. Permanent fix: Rollback or patch PR #3283 to reintroduce parallel invalidation for residency stamps and add a short 'grace' routing window while propagation completes to avoid cross-region fallback. Assigned to INT-4412 for engineering fix and to infra for a follow-up postmortem. Customer agreed to keep affinity off until patch is deployed. Follow-ups: add instrumentation to detect mixing of egress paths for a single residency-change event and SLA-facing notification if propagation exceeds 30s.
